newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power slips on gas, milder temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic power slips on gas, milder temps.

text.p: Bulk electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. slipped Friday on a plummet in natural gas futures and forecast of milder temperatures moderating next week following the arctic system this weekend.
"Things should moderate next week," said an East Coast broker, referring to temperatures in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect district.

Firm, peak PJM electricity prices for Monday (excluding transmission costs) were quoted near $34.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) after traded as high as $40.00, down more than $10.00 from Thursday's $45.00-$50.00.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Monday delivery held in the $18.00-$20.00 range.

Temperatures in the PJM region were expected to average 15 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit below normal Friday through Sunday, with gusts pushing the wind chill factor well below zero. By Tuesday, PJM temperatures would run five degrees below normal.
Forward PJM values continued their decline along with another plunge in natural gas futures, market sources said.
As of 1219 EST, the NYMEX February Henry Hub gas contract fell 18.6 cents at $3.155 per million British thermal units, also on more moderate weather in the eastern U.S. next week.
PJM deliveries for the five business days next week traded at $32.00, compared with Thursday's offers near $33.00.
February PJM electricity was dropped to $29.50-$29.70, off about 25 cents from $29.75-$30.00 Thursday.
March PJM electricity edged down to $24.60-$24.80 from Thursday's quote of $24.75-$25.00.
PJM deliveries April and May stepped down to $22.10-$22.50 from $22.50-$22.75 Thursday.
June power prices in PJM slipped to $24.70-$25.00 from Thursday's $25.10-25.35.
July/August PJM electricity moved down to $31.15-$31.50 from $31.25-$31.40 Thursday.
Swing natgas prices at the Philadelphia city gate were notionally assessed at $4.50-$4.80/mmBtu, down from Thursday's $5.25 level amid falling spot prices in the Gulf Coast market.
